label: One grouped select
thesis: The genre picker is one more select in the existing filter strip, with each main genre as a group whose first entry is 'All Jazz' and its sub-genres beneath. It matches the geo filter's pattern and costs the least space and code.
risk: A long grouped list of sub-genres is hard to scan in a native select, especially on a phone, and a main genre and its sub-genre are picked from one flat menu, so the choice is easy to misread.

label: Main genres, then sub-genres
thesis: A row of main-genre chips sits under the filter strip; choosing one opens a second row of its sub-genres with 'All Jazz' first. Everything visible at once, no menus, and the two levels are plain to see.
risk: Takes two rows of vertical space above the listing on the calendar and /bands, pushes the shows down, and wraps awkwardly on narrow screens; it departs from the strip's select-based style.

label: Genre rail with counts
thesis: A left rail lists main genres with counts, expanding the chosen one to show its sub-genres. Counts show what the filter will find before a visitor clicks, which suits a thin tagged dataset.
risk: Counts need extra queries per page, a rail costs listing width on a page that is dense and text-first, and on narrow screens it must collapse above the listing.
